question: Assess whether NAB's FY25 Business & Private Banking growth was value-accretive rather than growth bought at the expense of margin or credit quality. Reconcile lending, revenue and cash-earnings growth with the NIM, impairment-charge and sector/NPL disclosures, and identify what is broad-based versus single-name driven.
answer: NAB's FY25 Business & Private Banking (B&PB) growth was margin-accretive but credit-dilutive. B&PB cash earnings rose 1.6% to $3,330m, driven by volume growth and FX/wealth income, despite lower margins [ev-17]. Business lending balances grew 7.3%, outpacing the group’s 5.9% GLA growth [ev-3, ev-11], while deposits grew 6.6% [ev-12]. However, NIM declined 1bp ex-M&T/liquid assets due to deposit costs [ev-4]. Credit quality deteriorated: the default-but-not-impaired ratio rose 7bps, linked to B&PB business lending [ev-8]. Individually assessed impairment charges of $964m primarily related to this business lending portfolio [ev-9]. While collective provisions released $131m, the net charge increased 14.4% YoY [ev-7]. Thus, earnings growth relied on volume and non-interest income, offsetting a margin headwind and higher specific credit costs.

key_facts.fact: B&PB cash earnings grew 1.6% to $3,330m in FY25, supported by volume and FX/wealth income.
Business lending balances grew 7.3% in FY25, contributing to group GLA growth of 5.9%.
Group NIM declined 1bp ex-M&T and liquid assets, pressured by higher deposit costs.
Individually assessed impairment charges of $964m primarily related to the business lending portfolio.
The default-but-not-impaired ratio rose 7bps, mainly relating to B&PB business lending.

limitations: Specific B&PB NIM figures are not provided in the evidence records, only group-level and divisional cash earnings. The analysis infers margin pressure from group data and narrative statements.

evidence_records.quote: Net interest income increased by $644 million or 3.8%. This includes a decrease of $74 million due to movements in economic hedges, offset in other operating income. Excluding this movement, the underlying increase of $718 million or 4.3% was due to higher average interest earning assets and net interest margin.

Average interest earning assets increased by $22.5 billion or 2.3% reflecting growth primarily in business lending and, to a lesser extent, in housing lending, partially offset by a reduction in high-quality liquid assets (HQLA).

The Group's net interest margin increased by 3 basis points due to: an increase of 9 basis points mainly driven by higher earnings on deposit and capital replicating portfolios, an increase of 2 basis points driven by a lower mix of lower yielding HQLA, and an increase of 2 basis points in Markets and Treasury.
